lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are not relevant to evaluating the candidate’s work and are not expected in this résumé.

items.says: Crescent Bank appears above the more recent Stonebridge Manufacturing role.
items.because: The order is not newest-first and makes the career timeline harder to scan.

items.says: Education appears before the work history despite several years of professional experience.
items.because: The degree leads instead of the more recent and relevant employment.

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund entry is longer than needed.
items.because: Its several bullets take space from more recent professional work.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not hedge the existing holdings’ interest-rate risk.
items.because: The additional bonds generally add to that exposure rather than offsetting it.

items.says: The pronoun “my” does not belong in this résumé bullet.
“Writes” conflicts with the role dates ending in December 2022.
items.because: The present tense implies ongoing work in an ended role.

items.says: “Letting treasury pay down” states the debt-reduction result indirectly.
“So every request used the same” overstates what the shared template ensures and buries the outcome.
items.because: Users can change inputs or depart from the rules, so the template alone does not establish that every request followed them.

items.says: “Mapping” conflicts with the past-tense account of this ended role.
items.because: It leaves the bullet without a clear past-tense opening action and makes the timing unclear.

items.says: The reduction in manual entries appears after lengthy mapping and testing details.
items.because: That makes the result easy to miss.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC uses the wrong discount rate.
items.because: Equity cash flow should be discounted at the cost of equity; WACC is generally used for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The valuation bullet gives no outcome from the analysis.
The training and user-guide bullet gives no result of that support.
The market-price comparison gives no reference date.
items.because: A share price changes over time, so the 6% result is harder to interpret.

items.says: The 6% result comes after the methods.
items.because: That delays the most scannable outcome.

items.says: A fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is a 20% drop, not 25%.
items.because: The USD 10 decrease is 20% of the starting USD 50 value.

items.says: “1 point” does not specify whether the discount rate rose by one percentage point.
The increase from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points, not 12%.
items.because: A 12% increase misstates the change; the relative increase is about 17.1%.

items.says: The bullet does not define “forecast accuracy” or explain how the figures were evaluated.
items.because: Without the metric and comparison basis, a reader cannot interpret or assess the improvement.

items.says: “Supported the FP&A team with” frames the work as assistance rather than naming what was done.
The opening bullet gives no outcome or evidence of value.
“FP&A” may be unfamiliar to readers outside finance.
The bullet does not say what the performance report enabled the committee to do.
“Which the committee used at every meeting” puts the result after the action and makes “which” ambiguous.
The onboarding-notes bullet gives no result or evidence of how many people used the notes.
The Student Investment Fund bullets read as separate reporting and onboarding contributions rather than one focused piece of work.
